Read a Julia value

Source: R/guest-julia.R
jl_value.Rd

jl_value() reads a value that a Julia chunk made, in prose or in R code, and checks it as weft checks every value that reaches prose (rules 1.11 and 2.12.15). Each argument is one string, a step of a path: jl_value("n") reads the global n of Julia's Main; jl_value("cfg", "depth") reads cfg, then its key depth when cfg is a dictionary (a String key, else the Symbol key), else its field depth. Only the last value is read.

Usage

jl_value(...)

Arguments

...

One or more non-empty strings: the name in Julia's Main, then the keys or fields below it.

Value

The R form of the value: a logical, integer or double, a character string, a Date, or an atomic vector of one of these for a list, named for a NamedTuple. A missing value is NA.

Details

The value is read inside Julia from its type, never by JuliaCall's conversion, which stops on a whole number beyond 2^31, hands a UInt8 over as a raw vector and ends R on a missing. A Bool, an integer, a float (Float16, Float32 and Float64, widened exactly), a string, a Char, a Symbol, a Dates.Date and a vector or tuple of one of these (a NamedTuple with names) are read. An integer beyond 2^53, a Rational, an Irrational, a BigFloat, a DateTime, a dictionary, a set, a matrix and anything else are refused with a weft_guest_value_error that says what to do. missing, nothing, NaN and infinities are NA.

In an attribute value the argument takes single quotes: {if="jl_value('ok')"}. When Julia is not running, jl_value() starts it with JuliaCall::julia_setup() and defines weft's one module, WeftGuest, in Julia's Main. weft never installs Julia or a Julia package.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs Julia, which takes a few seconds to start
JuliaCall::julia_setup()
JuliaCall::julia_command("depth = 3.14159;")
jl_value("depth")
} # }
